From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: ACME - Follow-up: subprocessor list & SOC 2 status

Hi Tom — looping in answers to the questions and a few clarifications inline.

1) Regions: Redwood hosts customer inference workloads in US and EU regions by default. For customers that require EU-only residency we can pin workloads to our EU region (GCP-EU and AWS-EU zones). We do not persist customer content in APAC by default.

2) APAC subcontractors: We do not use APAC-based subprocessors to process customer payloads for EU-resident workloads. Global infra/support uses providers listed in the attached CSV (AWS, GCP, CloudSQL). We occasionally use a third-party logging/monitoring provider (Datadog) that receives metrics; logs containing customer content are redacted before leaving the runtime.

3) Analytics/3rd-party access: We use Segment/Datadog for telemetry but do not send raw customer payloads. Any user-level telemetry is hashed and pseudonymized; full request/response payloads are stored only in encrypted S3 buckets when customers opt-in to usage analytics.

Encryption & KMS: we encrypt at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.2+). Customer encryption keys can be managed via KMS (customer-managed keys supported for Private deployments). HSM integrations available for enterprise plans.

Data sharing boundaries: Redwood only shares customer content with subprocessors listed in the CSV when necessary to provide the service (e.g., storage, database, logging). We don't sell or otherwise transfer customer content.

Next steps: Marissa — please propose 2 slots for the technical Q&A. Tom — if you prefer, we can also fill in the questionnaire directly; I can take the technical sections.

Links: HubSpot deal RDW-4521 (https://hubspot.example.com/deal/4521) and detailed subprocessor mapping (https://drive.google.com/open?id=redwood-acme-subprocessors-map).

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Infra & Security Lead
Redwood Inference
